what_it_does: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is a technique for rendering photorealistic 3D scenes in real time, but it currently runs at only 2–9 frames per second on mobile devices when 90 FPS is needed for smooth viewing. While previous accelerators improved the compute efficiency, they ignored memory efficiency—causing the system to waste time repeatedly fetching the same data from memory. STREAMINGGS fixes this by redesigning both the algorithm and hardware together. Instead of loading all 3D scene elements (called Gaussians) into cache and then deciding which parts to render, it streams Gaussian groups and only loads the specific image tiles each group will touch. This dramatically reduces redundant memory traffic and enables better memory prediction on mobile GPUs.
